title: Audio loudness targets, subtitle standards and frame rates for video editors (2026)
notes: Every value was taken from the source(s) listed on its row, opened between 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13. 'official' = published by the platform or standards body; 'industry' = third-party measurement or summary; 'own measurement' = shortformkit.com study. LUFS and LKFS are the same unit. Dialogue-gated targets (Netflix, Amazon Studios) are not directly comparable with full-programme integrated measurements (EBU R 128, Spotify). null = no reliable value found.

loudness_targets.name: Spotify
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Playback normalization target for Premium 'Normal' setting; 'Loud' = -11 LUFS, 'Quiet' = -19 LUFS. Measured per ITU-R BS.1770. Album normalization when an album is played (gain constant across tracks), track normalization when shuffling or mixing albums. Quiet masters ARE turned up (positive gain, limited by headroom); in 'Loud' mode a limiter engages at -1 dB (sample values), 5 ms attack, 100 ms decay. Recommended master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak below -1 dBTP; if the master is louder than -14 LUFS keep true peak below -2 dBTP.

sources.title: Loudness normalization on Spotify

loudness_targets.name: Apple Music (Sound Check)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Apple's own document confirms Sound Check stores loudness in metadata, raises or lowers each track, and can work per album, but publishes no LUFS number. The -16 LUFS reference comes from industry measurement (Ian Shepherd, 2022: Apple follows AES TD1008 and normalizes music to -16 LUFS; Sound Check on by default only on new iOS/macOS installs). Apple recommends leaving at least 1 dB of headroom to avoid clipping from oversampling/encoding (not a stated true-peak spec).

sources.title: Apple Digital Masters (technology brief)
Apple switch to LUFS (MeterPlugs / Ian Shepherd, 2022-03-23)

loudness_targets.name: YouTube (incl. Shorts)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: No official YouTube Help page publishes a loudness target. -14 LUFS is the industry-measured playback reference (changed quietly in 2019); YouTube turns loud videos down but does not turn quiet videos up. The applied gain is visible in 'Stats for nerds' (content loudness). Because normalization happens at playback, delivered files are not levelled: shortformkit.com measured 41 non-silent YouTube Shorts files (2026-10-12) at median -19.6 LUFS, 22% louder than -12 LUFS, 34% with true peak above -1 dBTP.

sources.title: YouTube changes loudness reference to -14 LUFS (MeterPlugs / Ian Shepherd, 2019-09-18)
Short-form video quality study 2026 (shortformkit.com, 135 public Reels/TikToks/Shorts measured 2026-10-12)

loudness_targets.name: Amazon Music
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: No public Amazon Music for Artists loudness document was found. -14 LUFS is from industry measurement (MeterPlugs, 2019). Industry guides also state Amazon only turns loud content down and recommend -2 dBTP; unconfirmed by Amazon. The only official Amazon loudness doc found is for Alexa skills/Flash Briefings: average -14 LUFS/LKFS, rejected below -19 or above -9 LUFS, true peak not above -2 dBFS (that spec is not Amazon Music).

sources.title: Loudness Penalty adds Amazon and Deezer (MeterPlugs, 2019-10-15)
LUFS Loudness Standards for 50+ Platforms (Dan Murtagh, specs reviewed July 2026)
Normalizing the Loudness of Audio Content | Alexa Skills Kit

loudness_targets.name: TIDAL
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Album normalization: the loudest track of each album is normalized to -14 LUFS and other tracks keep their relative level; measured per ITU-R BS.1770-4. Only attenuates, never applies positive gain, so quiet albums play quiet. Source is a 2017 report of TIDAL's implementation; TIDAL's former support article (360013379377) now returns 'page doesn't exist', so current behaviour is not officially confirmed.

sources.title: Tidal Implements Album Loudness Normalization and Activates It by Default for Mobile Players (audioXpress, 2017-11-27)

loudness_targets.name: Deezer
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Deezer's help page confirms volume normalization exists on iOS, Android and Desktop and can be toggled off, but gives no LUFS value. -15 LUFS is from industry measurement (MeterPlugs, 2019). Track vs album normalization not documented officially.

sources.title: Volume Normalization on Deezer
Loudness Penalty adds Amazon and Deezer (MeterPlugs, 2019-10-15)

loudness_targets.name: SoundCloud
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Official mastering tip: master at -14 LUFS integrated with true peak below -1 dBTP (best for its lossy formats Ogg/Vorbis and AAC); if louder than -14 LUFS keep true peak below -2 dBTP. SoundCloud states it applies loudness normalization at playback but the page does not state the normalization level or whether quiet tracks are raised.

sources.title: Will SoundCloud play my track at the level it's mastered? - SoundCloud Help Center

loudness_targets.name: Netflix (branded content, near-field mixes)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Average loudness -27 LKFS, dialog-gated, measured over the full program per ITU-R BS.1770-1. Peaks must not exceed -2 dBTP. Applies to Netflix branded content; licensed content follows the separate Full Non-Branded Delivery Specification. Note: dialog-gated -27 is not comparable with full-program (ungated-to-dialogue) integrated LUFS readings.

sources.title: Netflix Branded Sound Mix Specifications & Best Practices (Netflix Studio Partner Knowledge Hub; formerly Partner Help Center article 360001794307)

loudness_targets.name: Amazon Prime Video / Amazon MGM Studios productions
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Amazon Studios portal: Near Field 5.1/2.0 mixes, loudness target -27 LKFS ±2 LU, measured with BS.1770-1 plus dialogue gating (Dolby Dialogue Intelligence); max true peak -2 dBTP; QC rejects outside -27 ±2 LU. Dolby Atmos audio has no loudness requirement. DISAGREEMENT: several industry references list Prime Video as -24 LKFS / -2 dBTP; the public Prime Video Direct/Video Central tech docs list no loudness value at all, so the -24 figure may stem from older or licensed-content specs.

loudness_targets.name: Disney+
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: No public official Disney+ loudness spec could be opened (Disney Media Tech Specs portal did not render audio content). Values are from one industry compilation only (-27 LKFS dialogue-gated, -2 dBTP). Treat as unverified.

loudness_targets.name: EBU R 128 (European broadcast)
loudness_targets.tolerance: ±1.0 LU only where the target is not practically achievable (e.g. live); ±0.2 LU allowed for measurement error in QC
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: R 128-2023 (v5.0, Nov 2023): normalise Programme Loudness to -23.0 LUFS, gated measurement per ITU-R BS.1770 and EBU Tech 3341, measured over the whole programme without emphasis on speech, music or effects (not dialogue-gated). Max true peak -1 dBTP in production (linear audio), lower limits may apply for distribution (EBU Tech 3344). Loudness Range per Tech 3342; production guidance in Tech 3343. DISAGREEMENT: v3.0 (2014) set a ±0.5 LU target tolerance; v4.0 (2020) updated tolerances, and many meter presets (e.g. iZotope) still show ±0.5 LU.

loudness_targets.name: EBU R 128 s1 (short-form: ads, promos)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Programme Loudness -23.0 LUFS; Maximum Short-term Loudness (3 s window) must not exceed -18.0 LUFS (+5 LU); Loudness Range not applicable. Short-form = up to approx. 2 minutes, typically under 30 s.

sources.title: EBU R 128 s1 Loudness Parameters for Short-form Content (Adverts, Promos etc.)

loudness_targets.name: EBU R 128 s2 (broadcasters' streaming)
loudness_targets.tolerance: interim Distribution Loudness -20.0 to -16.0 LUFS allowed if no loudness metadata is used
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: R 128 s2-2023: programmes produced per R 128 should be streamed unchanged at -23.0 LUFS with correct loudness metadata; without metadata, the Distribution Loudness Level may be raised to -20 to -16 LUFS. Devices that raise level should apply true-peak limiting per EBU Tech 3344. References AES71 (OTT video) and AES77 (audio streaming).

sources.title: EBU R 128 s2-2023 Loudness in Streaming

loudness_targets.name: ATSC A/85 (US broadcast, CALM Act)
loudness_targets.tolerance: ±2 dB (measurement variation; content should not be targeted to either side)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Target Loudness -24 LKFS for delivery/exchange without metadata; true peak kept below -2 dBTP. Long-form content: measure the Anchor Element (typically dialogue) per BS.1770, else full-program integrated loudness. Short-form (ads, interstitials): full-program integrated loudness. A/85:2013 (approved 12 March 2013).

loudness_targets.name: ARIB TR-B32 (Japan broadcast)
loudness_targets.tolerance: ±2 LU (industry preset; not verified in the official text)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Operational guidelines for loudness of Japanese digital TV, measured per ITU-R BS.1770-3/-4 with gating. ARIB lists v1.7 dated 10.09.2026 as latest. The official numeric values could not be opened (the free sample PDF contains only the table of contents); -24 LKFS, ±2 LU and -1 dBTP come from iZotope's preset table. Other secondary sources quote ±1 LU, so the tolerance is uncertain.

loudness_targets.name: AES TD1004.1.15-10 (2015, superseded)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: AES recommendation for audio streaming and network file playback: target window -16 to -20 LUFS, max true peak -1 dBTP. Superseded by TD1008 (2021) and AES77-2023. Official PDF is behind a bot check, values taken from industry coverage.

loudness_targets.name: AES TD1008 / AES77-2023 (speech, podcasts)
loudness_targets.tolerance: +2 LU upper tolerance for speech (industry summary)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Distribution Loudness for speech and 'assorted' content -18 LUFS; mixed music+speech streams may sit at -17 LUFS (within the speech tolerance). TD1008 (2021) became the AES Recommended Practice AES77 in July 2023. Official text not opened (AES site bot check; AES77 is paywalled), so true-peak value not verified.

loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Distribution Loudness for music -16 LUFS (TD1008 gives two methods, track-based and album/anchor-based, that give the same overall result per Production Advice). Apple Music's -16 LUFS reference is reported to follow this.

loudness_targets.name: Apple Podcasts
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: Recommended: overall loudness around -16 LKFS ±1 dB, true peak not exceeding -1 dBFS, both per ITU-R BS.1770-5. Preconditioning must happen before encoding.

loudness_targets.name: Audible / ACX (audiobooks)
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: ACX does not specify LUFS. Requirements: each file -23 to -18 dB RMS, peak values no higher than -3 dB (peak, not specified as true peak), noise floor no higher than -60 dB RMS, 1 to 5 s room tone at head/tail, max 120 min per file, 192 kbps+ CBR 44.1 kHz MP3, all files mono or all stereo.

loudness_targets.name: Instagram Reels
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: No official Meta/Instagram loudness spec exists. Industry recommendation: -14 LUFS, -1 dBTP; Meta uses xHE-AAC with adaptive loudness management. Own measurement (2026-10-12): 92% of 50 non-silent public Reels were within ±1 LU of -14 LUFS, median -14.1, loudest -14.0 LUFS, none louder than -12; median true peak -0.8 dBTP. This pattern suggests Instagram turns loud uploads down to about -14 LUFS at processing time; undocumented by Instagram.

loudness_targets.name: TikTok
loudness_targets.measurement_notes: No official TikTok loudness spec exists; industry sources call the common '-14 LUFS' figure a guess. Own measurement (2026-10-12) of 42 public TikToks: delivered files are not levelled, median -21.2 LUFS, 80% between -27.5 and -15.0 LUFS, only 10% within ±1 LU of -14, median true peak -6.6 dBTP. Practical advice from the study: master to about -14 LUFS so videos do not sound weaker than others.
